paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּהַ֥ר סִינַ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And YHWH spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,

notes.official: *bəhar sînay* 'on Mount Sinai' (central `har-sinai-horev-the-mountain-of-Elohim-divine-mountain-cross-corpus`). Lev 25-26 are set on the mountain (26:46; cf. 27:34), while the laws from Lev 1:1 onward are given from the tent of meeting. This is one of the literary seams of the book (Milgrom, *Leviticus 23-27*, AB 3B, 2001).

paragraphs.text: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֤י תָבֹ֙אוּ֙ אֶל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֣ן לָכֶ֑ם וְשָׁבְתָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: "Speak to the children of Yisra'el and say to them, 'When you come into the land which I am giving you, then the land shall keep a Sabbath to YHWH.

notes.official: *wəšāḇəṯâ hāʾāreṣ šabbāṯ laYHWH* 'then the land shall keep a Sabbath to YHWH': the land itself is the subject of the Sabbath, as it is the one that 'enjoys its Sabbaths' in 26:34-35. 'Sabbath' is capitalised as in exodus-woh (16:23-29; 20:8-11), where NRSV and NJPS print lower case. *hāʾāreṣ* is 'the land' throughout the chapter, the territory YHWH gives (central `eretz`). YHWH's speech to Moses is in double quotation marks, and the law Moses is to speak to the people, YHWH's first-person address, is in single marks, running to v 55 (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: שֵׁ֤שׁ שָׁנִים֙ תִּזְרַ֣ע שָׂדֶ֔ךָ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְמֹ֣ר כַּרְמֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather in its produce;

notes.official: *təḇûʾāṯāh* 'its produce': the yield of the land as a mass noun (overlay `lexical-cruxes-leviticus-25`). The count plural of vv 15-16 is rendered 'crops'. *tizmōr* 'prune'.

paragraphs.text: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗ת שַׁבַּ֤ת שַׁבָּתוֹן֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָאָ֔רֶץ שַׁבָּ֖ת לַיהוָ֑ה שָֽׂדְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תִזְרָ֔ע וְכַרְמְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תִזְמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a Sabbath to YHWH; you shall not sow your field, nor prune your vineyard.

notes.official: *šabbaṯ šabbāṯôn* 'a Sabbath of solemn rest' (ASV): a superlative construct like *qōḏeš qŏḏāšîm*, 'a Sabbath of complete rest' (NRSV, NJPS), under overlay `shofar-teruah-yovel-deror-jubilee-leviticus-25`. exodus-woh 16:23 renders the bare *šabbāṯôn* 'a Sabbath observance', and the two renderings are to be reconciled at the next Torah pass. Ex 23:10-11 gives the seventh-year fallow a social reason (the poor and the wild animals eat); Lev 25 adds a theological one: the land rests 'to YHWH'.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֣ת סְפִ֤יחַ קְצִֽירְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תִקְצ֔וֹר וְאֶת־עִנְּבֵ֥י נְזִירֶ֖ךָ לֹ֣א תִבְצֹ֑ר שְׁנַ֥ת שַׁבָּת֖וֹן יִהְיֶ֥ה לָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: What grows of itself from your harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your untrimmed vine you shall not gather; it shall be a year of solemn rest for the land.

notes.official: *sp̄îaḥ qəṣîrəḵā* 'what grows of itself from your harvest': the self-sown aftergrowth. *ʿinnəḇê nəzîreḵā* 'the grapes of your untrimmed vine': *nāzîr* is the word for the Nazirite, so the unpruned vine is left uncut as the Nazirite's hair is (Num 6:5; Milgrom, AB 3B). *šənaṯ šabbāṯôn* 'a year of solemn rest' (overlay `shofar-teruah-yovel-deror-jubilee-leviticus-25`).

paragraphs.text: וְ֠הָיְתָה שַׁבַּ֨ת הָאָ֤רֶץ לָכֶם֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה לְךָ֖ וּלְעַבְדְּךָ֣ וְלַאֲמָתֶ֑ךָ וְלִשְׂכִֽירְךָ֙ וּלְתוֹשָׁ֣בְךָ֔ הַגָּרִ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And the Sabbath of the land shall be food for you: for you, and for your male slave and for your female slave, and for your hired worker and for your resident, who sojourn with you;

notes.official: *wəhāyəṯâ šabbaṯ hāʾāreṣ lāḵem ləʾoḵlâ* 'the Sabbath of the land shall be food for you': what the land yields of itself in its Sabbath year. Vv 5-6 forbid organised harvesting, not eating. *ləʿaḇdəḵā wəlaʾămāṯeḵā* 'for your male slave and for your female slave' (ASV 'thy servant and thy maid'): the household list takes the same English pair as v 44, under overlay `eved-amah-slave-servant-leviticus-25`. *śəḵîrəḵā* 'your hired worker'; *tôšāḇəḵā* 'your resident' (ASV 'thy stranger'), a dependent resident without land (overlay `ger-toshav-sojourner-resident-leviticus-25`); *haggārîm ʿimmāḵ* 'who sojourn with you' (central `megurim-patriarchal-sojourner-self-identity-gur-root`).

paragraphs.text: וְלִ֨בְהֶמְתְּךָ֔ וְלַֽחַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאַרְצֶ֑ךָ תִּהְיֶ֥ה כָל־תְּבוּאָתָ֖הּ לֶאֱכֹֽל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: and for your cattle, and for the wild animals that are in your land: all its produce shall be for food.

notes.official: *wəlaḥayyâ ʾăšer bəʾarṣeḵā* 'and for the wild animals that are in your land' (cf. Ex 23:11).

paragraphs.text: וְסָפַרְתָּ֣ לְךָ֗ שֶׁ֚בַע שַׁבְּתֹ֣ת שָׁנִ֔ים שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וְהָי֣וּ לְךָ֗ יְמֵי֙ שֶׁ֚בַע שַׁבְּתֹ֣ת הַשָּׁנִ֔ים תֵּ֥שַׁע וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And you shall count for yourself seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years; and the days of the seven Sabbaths of years shall be to you forty-nine years.

notes.official:
*šeḇaʿ šabbəṯōṯ šānîm* 'seven Sabbaths of years': *šabbāṯ* here names a seven-year unit, the 'week of years' (cf. Dan 9:24-27). Seven of them make forty-nine years, and the fiftieth is the jubilee (v 10). Whether the fiftieth year is a separate year or coincides with the first year of the next cycle is debated (Milgrom, AB 3B; Bergsma, *The Jubilee from Leviticus to Qumran*, 2007).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 6) quotes vv 8, 14-16 and 23 ('Thou shalt count for thee seven sabbaths of years, seven times seven years: (…) forty-nine years … the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine, while you are guests and residents with me', 'Leviticus, XXV, 8, 14-16, 23'). The book cites them as the biblical precedent of its proposal that all goods belong to the community and that a person may lease property for no more than forty-nine years, after which it returns to the community. The line renders the count, the price rule and the land law as the Hebrew states them and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וְהַֽעֲבַרְתָּ֞ שׁוֹפַ֤ר תְּרוּעָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֖וֹר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בְּיוֹם֙ הַכִּפֻּרִ֔ים תַּעֲבִ֥ירוּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר בְּכָל־אַרְצְכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Then you shall sound abroad a shofar blast in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month; on the Day of Atonement you shall sound the shofar abroad throughout all your land.

notes.official: *wəhaʿăḇartā šôp̄ar tərûʿâ* 'Then you shall sound abroad a shofar blast': literally 'you shall make a shofar of blasting pass through' (ASV 'send abroad the loud trumpet'). 'shofar' follows central `shofar-rams-horn-signal-instrument-cross-corpus`. *tərûʿâ* is here the horn signal of Num 10:5-9 and Lev 23:24, not the people's war cry that joshua-woh renders 'shout' (overlay `shofar-teruah-yovel-deror-jubilee-leviticus-25`). The construct has no article, so the line has 'a shofar blast'. *bəyôm hakkippurîm* 'on the Day of Atonement' (Lev 16:29-34; 23:27), capitalised as a fixed festival name (NRSV, NJPS; ASV lower case). The jubilee is proclaimed on the tenth day of the seventh month, the day of the annual purgation.

paragraphs.text: וְקִדַּשְׁתֶּ֗ם אֵ֣ת שְׁנַ֤ת הַחֲמִשִּׁים֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וּקְרָאתֶ֥ם דְּר֛וֹר בָּאָ֖רֶץ לְכָל־יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ יוֹבֵ֥ל הִוא֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם וְשַׁבְתֶּ֗ם אִ֚ישׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזָּת֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֶל־מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ תָּשֻֽׁבוּ׃

i18n.en: And you shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants; it shall be a jubilee to you, and you shall return each man to his possession, and you shall return each man to his family.

notes.official:
*ûqrāʾṯem dərôr bāʾāreṣ ləḵol-yōšəḇeyhā* 'and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants'. *dərôr* is cognate with Akkadian *andurāru*, the royal decree that released debts and debt-slaves and returned land (CAD A/II, *andurāru*). The word recurs in Jer 34:8-17, Isa 61:1 and Ezek 46:17. 'liberty' (ASV, NRSV; NJPS 'release') is kept. The KJV wording of this clause is inscribed on the Liberty Bell in Philadelphia.

*yôḇēl hîʾ* 'it shall be a jubilee': *yôḇēl* is the ram and the ram's horn in Ex 19:13 and Josh 6 (central shofar-rams-horn-signal-instrument-cross-corpus, 'ram's horn'). Here it names the year that the horn proclaimed, and the year keeps the established English 'jubilee' (overlay `shofar-teruah-yovel-deror-jubilee-leviticus-25`). *ʾîš ʾel-ʾăḥuzzāṯô* 'each man to his possession' (central `achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword`).

paragraphs.text: יוֹבֵ֣ל הִ֗וא שְׁנַ֛ת הַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תִזְרָ֔עוּ וְלֹ֤א תִקְצְרוּ֙ אֶת־סְפִיחֶ֔יהָ וְלֹ֥א תִבְצְר֖וּ אֶת־נְזִרֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: That fiftieth year shall be a jubilee to you; you shall not sow, nor reap what grows of itself in it, nor gather the grapes of its untrimmed vines.

notes.official: The fiftieth year repeats the fallow of the seventh (vv 4-5): no sowing, reaping or vintage.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֚י יוֹבֵ֣ל הִ֔וא קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם מִן־הַ֨שָּׂדֶ֔ה תֹּאכְל֖וּ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy to you; you shall eat its produce out of the field.

notes.official: *qōḏeš tihyeh lāḵem* 'it shall be holy to you'. *min-haśśāḏeh tōʾḵəlû* 'you shall eat its produce out of the field': directly from the field, without harvesting into storage.

paragraphs.text: בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הַיּוֹבֵ֖ל הַזֹּ֑את תָּשֻׁ֕בוּ אִ֖ישׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: In this year of jubilee you shall return each man to his possession.

notes.official: The return 'each man to his possession' (central `achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword`) is the core of the jubilee: land sold during the cycle reverts to its family.

paragraphs.text: וְכִֽי־תִמְכְּר֤וּ מִמְכָּר֙ לַעֲמִיתֶ֔ךָ א֥וֹ קָנֹ֖ה מִיַּ֣ד עֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ אַל־תּוֹנ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִֽיו׃

i18n.en: And if you sell anything to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor's hand, you shall not wrong one another.

notes.official: *ʿămîṯeḵā* 'your neighbor', the fellow member of the community (ASV 'thy neighbor'). *ʾal-tônû ʾîš ʾeṯ-ʾāḥîw* 'you shall not wrong one another': *hônâ* is to cheat or oppress. Vv 14-16 are quoted in *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 6); see the reception note at v 8. The canon's English agrees with the line in substance.

paragraphs.text: בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שָׁנִים֙ אַחַ֣ר הַיּוֹבֵ֔ל תִּקְנֶ֖ה מֵאֵ֣ת עֲמִיתֶ֑ךָ בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר שְׁנֵֽי־תְבוּאֹ֖ת יִמְכָּר־לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: According to the number of years after the jubilee you shall buy from your neighbor; according to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.

notes.official: *bəmispar šənê-ṯəḇûʾōṯ* 'according to the number of years of crops': the count plural of *təḇûʾâ* names the harvests the buyer will take before the jubilee (overlay `lexical-cruxes-leviticus-25`; ASV and the canon quotation 'crops'; NRSV 'harvests'). A sale of land is therefore in effect a lease of its harvests until the land reverts.

paragraphs.text: לְפִ֣י ׀ רֹ֣ב הַשָּׁנִ֗ים תַּרְבֶּה֙ מִקְנָת֔וֹ וּלְפִי֙ מְעֹ֣ט הַשָּׁנִ֔ים תַּמְעִ֖יט מִקְנָת֑וֹ כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר תְּבוּאֹ֔ת ה֥וּא מֹכֵ֖ר לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: According to the many years you shall increase its price, and according to the few years you shall diminish its price; for it is a number of crops that he is selling to you.

notes.official: *kî mispar təḇûʾōṯ hûʾ mōḵēr lāḵ* 'for it is a number of crops that he is selling to you': the price rises with the years remaining before the jubilee and falls as they decrease. The canon's English ('for it is a number of crops that he sells to thee') matches the line.

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֤א תוֹנוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־עֲמִית֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵֽאֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And you shall not wrong one another, but you shall fear your Elohim; for I am YHWH your Elohim.

notes.official: *wəyārēʾṯā mēʾĕlōheyḵā* 'but you shall fear your Elohim' (central `yirat-elohim-moral-restraint-motif`; `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`, clause 2). The fear of the deity restrains where no human court can see, as in the other occurrences of the formula in Lev 19 and 25 (19:14, 32; 25:36, 43). *kî ʾănî YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵem* 'for I am YHWH your Elohim'.

paragraphs.text: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֙ אֶת־חֻקֹּתַ֔י וְאֶת־מִשְׁפָּטַ֥י תִּשְׁמְר֖וּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אֹתָ֑ם וִֽישַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ לָבֶֽטַח׃

i18n.en: And you shall do my statutes and keep my ordinances and do them, and you shall dwell in the land in safety.

notes.official: *wîšaḇtem ʿal-hāʾāreṣ lāḇeṭaḥ* 'and you shall dwell in the land in safety': security in the land is conditional on keeping the statutes, the theme of Lev 26:3-13.

paragraphs.text: וְנָתְנָ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ פִּרְיָ֔הּ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֖ם לָשֹׂ֑בַע וִֽישַׁבְתֶּ֥ם לָבֶ֖טַח עָלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And the land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat your fill and dwell in it in safety.

paragraphs.text: וְכִ֣י תֹאמְר֔וּ מַה־נֹּאכַ֤֖ל בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑ת הֵ֚ן לֹ֣א נִזְרָ֔ע וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱסֹ֖ף אֶת־תְּבוּאָתֵֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: And if you say, "What shall we eat in the seventh year? Behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our produce,"

notes.official: The people's anticipated objection is quoted in double marks inside YHWH's speech (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וְצִוִּ֤יתִי אֶת־בִּרְכָתִי֙ לָכֶ֔ם בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֑ית וְעָשָׂת֙ אֶת־הַתְּבוּאָ֔ה לִשְׁלֹ֖שׁ הַשָּׁנִֽים׃

i18n.en: then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth produce for the three years.

notes.official: *wəṣiwwîṯî ʾeṯ-birḵāṯî* 'I will command my blessing': the sixth-year harvest will be enough 'for the three years', the sixth, the fallow seventh and the eighth until its harvest comes in (v 22). How the count works when the forty-ninth and fiftieth years are both fallow is not stated (Milgrom, AB 3B).

paragraphs.text: וּזְרַעְתֶּ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁמִינִ֔ת וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֖ם מִן־הַתְּבוּאָ֣ה יָשָׁ֑ן עַ֣ד ׀ הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַתְּשִׁיעִ֗ת עַד־בּוֹא֙ תְּב֣וּאָתָ֔הּ תֹּאכְל֖וּ יָשָֽׁן׃

i18n.en: And you shall sow in the eighth year and eat from the old produce; until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, you shall eat the old.

notes.official: *yāšān* 'old': the stored produce of the sixth year.

paragraphs.text: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ לֹ֤א תִמָּכֵר֙ לִצְמִתֻ֔ת כִּי־לִ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֧ים וְתוֹשָׁבִ֛ים אַתֶּ֖ם עִמָּדִֽי׃

i18n.en: And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine; for you are sojourners and residents with me.

notes.official: *wəhāʾāreṣ lōʾ ṯimmāḵēr liṣmiṯuṯ* 'And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity' (ASV; NJPS 'beyond reclaim'; overlay `lexical-cruxes-leviticus-25`). *kî-lî hāʾāreṣ* 'for the land is mine' gives the reason. *kî-ḡērîm wəṯôšāḇîm ʾattem ʿimmāḏî* 'for you are sojourners and residents with me': Israel holds the land as YHWH's dependants, without title of its own (overlay `ger-toshav-sojourner-resident-leviticus-25`; central `megurim-patriarchal-sojourner-self-identity-gur-root`). The ASV has 'strangers and sojourners'. The same pair is Avraham's self-description in Gen 23:4, where genesis-woh prints the ASV pair 'a stranger and a sojourner', and it recurs in Ps 39:13 and 1 Chr 29:15. The English canon quotation has 'guests and residents' (*The Book Which Tells the Truth*, ch. 6; see the reception note at v 8).

paragraphs.text: וּבְכֹ֖ל אֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזַּתְכֶ֑ם גְּאֻלָּ֖ה תִּתְּנ֥וּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And in all the land of your possession you shall grant a redemption for the land.

notes.official: *gəʾullâ tittənû lāʾāreṣ* 'you shall grant a redemption for the land': every sale of family land carries the right of buy-back. The *gʾl* family is rendered with one English root throughout the chapter, 'redeem', 'redeemer', 'redemption' (central `goel-geullah-redeemer-redemption-cross-corpus`, proposed in this wave).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־יָמ֣וּךְ אָחִ֔יךָ וּמָכַ֖ר מֵאֲחֻזָּת֑וֹ וּבָ֤א גֹֽאֲלוֹ֙ הַקָּרֹ֣ב אֵלָ֔יו וְגָאַ֕ל אֵ֖ת מִמְכַּ֥ר אָחִֽיו׃

i18n.en: If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his possession, then his redeemer who is nearest to him shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.

notes.official: *ûḇāʾ gōʾălô haqqārōḇ ʾēlāyw wəḡāʾal* 'then his redeemer who is nearest to him shall come and redeem': the *gōʾēl* is the next of kin obliged to buy back family land and persons (vv 47-49; Ruth 3-4; Jer 32:6-15). The ASV has 'his kinsman that is next unto him', NJPS 'his nearest redeemer', NRSV 'the next of kin'. 'redeemer' keeps the noun's link with the verb, as in the Isaiah title 'your Redeemer' (Isa 43:14; 44:24) (central `goel-geullah-redeemer-redemption-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־לּ֖וֹ גֹּאֵ֑ל וְהִשִּׂ֣יגָה יָד֔וֹ וּמָצָ֖א כְּדֵ֥י גְאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And if a man has no one to redeem it, and he himself prospers and finds enough to redeem it,

notes.official: *wəhiśśîḡâ yāḏô* 'and he himself prospers': literally 'his hand reaches', i.e. he acquires the means. *kəḏê ḡəʾullāṯô* 'enough to redeem it'.

paragraphs.text: וְחִשַּׁב֙ אֶת־שְׁנֵ֣י מִמְכָּר֔וֹ וְהֵשִׁיב֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֹדֵ֔ף לָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָֽכַר־ל֑וֹ וְשָׁ֖ב לַאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: then he shall reckon the years since its sale, and restore the remainder to the man to whom he sold it; and he shall return to his possession.

notes.official: *wəḥiššaḇ ʾeṯ-šənê mimkārô* 'he shall reckon the years since its sale': the seller refunds the value of the harvests not yet taken before the jubilee.

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֨ם לֹֽא־מָֽצְאָ֜ה יָד֗וֹ דֵּי֮ הָשִׁ֣יב לוֹ֒ וְהָיָ֣ה מִמְכָּר֗וֹ בְּיַד֙ הַקֹּנֶ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיּוֹבֵ֑ל וְיָצָא֙ בַּיֹּבֵ֔ל וְשָׁ֖ב לַאֲחֻזָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: But if he has not found enough to restore it to him, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of him who bought it until the year of jubilee; and in the jubilee it shall go out, and he shall return to his possession.

notes.official: *wəyāṣāʾ bayyōḇēl* 'and in the jubilee it shall go out': *yāṣāʾ* is the technical verb for release, used of the land here and of persons in vv 41, 54 (cf. Ex 21:2).

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֗ישׁ כִּֽי־יִמְכֹּ֤ר בֵּית־מוֹשַׁב֙ עִ֣יר חוֹמָ֔ה וְהָיְתָה֙ גְּאֻלָּת֔וֹ עַד־תֹּ֖ם שְׁנַ֣ת מִמְכָּר֑וֹ יָמִ֖ים תִּהְיֶ֥ה גְאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And if a man sells a dwelling-house in a walled city, its redemption shall last until the end of a year after its sale; for a full year shall be its redemption.

notes.official: *bêṯ-môšaḇ ʿîr ḥômâ* 'a dwelling-house in a walled city': urban houses are not ancestral farmland, so the right of redemption lasts only one full year (*yāmîm*, here 'a full year', as in 1 Sam 27:7 and Judg 17:10).

paragraphs.text: וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא־יִגָּאֵ֗ל עַד־מְלֹ֣את לוֹ֮ שָׁנָ֣ה תְמִימָה֒ וְ֠קָם הַבַּ֨יִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִ֜יר אֲשֶׁר־לא [ל֣וֹ] חֹמָ֗ה לַצְּמִיתֻ֛ת לַקֹּנֶ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ לְדֹרֹתָ֑יו לֹ֥א יֵצֵ֖א בַּיֹּבֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And if it is not redeemed before a full year has passed for it, then the house that is in the city that has a wall shall stand in perpetuity to him who bought it, throughout his generations; it shall not go out in the jubilee.

notes.official: *ʾăšer-lô ḥômâ* 'that has a wall': the Ketiv writes *lʾ* 'not' ('which has no wall'), and the Qere reads *lô* 'to it' ('which has a wall'). The line translates the Qere, which the contrast with the unwalled villages of v 31 requires (ASV 'in the walled city'), under `mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`. *liṣmiṯuṯ* 'in perpetuity', as v 23. An unredeemed city house does not return in the jubilee.

paragraphs.text: וּבָתֵּ֣י הַחֲצֵרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֵין־לָהֶ֤ם חֹמָה֙ סָבִ֔יב עַל־שְׂדֵ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ יֵחָשֵׁ֑ב גְּאֻלָּה֙ תִּהְיֶה־לּ֔וֹ וּבַיֹּבֵ֖ל יֵצֵֽא׃

i18n.en: But the houses of the villages which have no wall around them shall be reckoned with the fields of the land; they shall have redemption, and they shall go out in the jubilee.

notes.official: *ûḇāttê haḥăṣērîm* 'the houses of the villages': unwalled settlements count as farmland, so they keep the right of redemption and return in the jubilee.

paragraphs.text: וְעָרֵי֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם בָּתֵּ֖י עָרֵ֣י אֲחֻזָּתָ֑ם גְּאֻלַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֖ם תִּהְיֶ֥ה לַלְוִיִּֽם׃

i18n.en: As for the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, the Levites shall have a perpetual redemption.

notes.official: *gəʾullaṯ ʿôlām* 'a perpetual redemption': the Levites, who hold no tribal territory (Num 18:20-24; 35:1-8), may redeem their city houses at any time.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר יִגְאַל֙ מִן־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם וְיָצָ֧א מִמְכַּר־בַּ֛יִת וְעִ֥יר אֲחֻזָּת֖וֹ בַּיֹּבֵ֑ל כִּ֣י בָתֵּ֞י עָרֵ֣י הַלְוִיִּ֗ם הִ֚וא אֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And if one of the Levites redeems, then the house that was sold in the city of his possession shall go out in the jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Yisra'el.

notes.official: *waʾăšer yiḡʾal min-hallᵊwiyyim* is difficult: literally 'and what one redeems from the Levites'. The line follows the ASV construal, 'And if one of the Levites redeems'. NJPS reads 'Such property as may be redeemed from the Levites', and the Vulgate and some commentators supply a negative ('if it is not redeemed') to match v 30. The MT is translated without emendation (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`; overlay `lexical-cruxes-leviticus-25`). *mimkar-bayiṯ wəʿîr ʾăḥuzzāṯô* is rendered 'the house that was sold in the city of his possession', taking the two nouns together (ASV 'the house that was sold, and the city of his possession').

paragraphs.text: וּֽשְׂדֵ֛ה מִגְרַ֥שׁ עָרֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א יִמָּכֵ֑ר כִּֽי־אֲחֻזַּ֥ת עוֹלָ֛ם ה֖וּא לָהֶֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: But the field of the open land of their cities shall not be sold, for it is a perpetual possession for them.

notes.official: *śəḏēh miḡraš ʿārêhem* 'the field of the open land of their cities': *miḡrāš* is the pasture belt around a town (Num 35:2-7). The ASV's 'suburbs' had that sense in older English but now means residential districts, so the line has 'open land' (NRSV; NJPS 'unenclosed land') (overlay `lexical-cruxes-leviticus-25`). *ʾăḥuzzaṯ ʿôlām* 'a perpetual possession'.

paragraphs.text: וְכִֽי־יָמ֣וּךְ אָחִ֔יךָ וּמָ֥טָה יָד֖וֹ עִמָּ֑ךְ וְהֶֽחֱזַ֣קְתָּ בּ֔וֹ גֵּ֧ר וְתוֹשָׁ֛ב וָחַ֖י עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And if your brother becomes poor and his hand falters beside you, then you shall support him; as a sojourner and a resident he shall live with you.

notes.official: *ûmāṭâ yāḏô ʿimmāḵ* 'and his hand falters beside you': he can no longer support himself. *wəheḥĕzaqtā bô* 'then you shall support him'. *gēr wəṯôšāḇ wāḥay ʿimmāḵ* 'as a sojourner and a resident he shall live with you': the impoverished Israelite is to be maintained as the law maintains the dependent resident (overlay `ger-toshav-sojourner-resident-leviticus-25`). The syntax is compressed, and NJPS reads 'and you hold him as though a resident alien, let him live by your side'.

paragraphs.text: אַל־תִּקַּ֤ח מֵֽאִתּוֹ֙ נֶ֣שֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּ֔ית וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵֽאֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְחֵ֥י אָחִ֖יךָ עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: Take no interest or increase from him, but fear your Elohim, that your brother may live with you.

notes.official: *nešeḵ wəṯarbîṯ* 'interest or increase': *nešeḵ* ('bite') is probably interest deducted in advance and *tarbîṯ* (v 37 *marbîṯ*) interest added at repayment (Milgrom, AB 3B). The pair is also forbidden in Ex 22:24 and Deut 23:20-21. *wəyārēʾṯā mēʾĕlōheyḵā* 'but fear your Elohim' (central `yirat-elohim-moral-restraint-motif`).

paragraphs.text: אֶ֨ת־כַּסְפְּךָ֔ לֹֽא־תִתֵּ֥ן ל֖וֹ בְּנֶ֑שֶׁךְ וּבְמַרְבִּ֖ית לֹא־תִתֵּ֥ן אָכְלֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: You shall not give him your money at interest, nor give him your food for increase.

paragraphs.text: אֲנִ֗י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לָתֵ֤ת לָכֶם֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן לִהְי֥וֹת לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ (ס)

i18n.en: I am YHWH your Elohim, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to give you the land of Canaan, to be your Elohim.

notes.official: 'Mitsrayim' = Egypt (central `mitsrayim`; `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`); 'the land of Canaan' (English form as numbers-woh 33:40, 51). *lihyôṯ lāḵem lēʾlōhîm* 'to be your Elohim': the covenant formula (Gen 17:7; Ex 6:7), under `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah`, clause 2.

paragraphs.text: וְכִֽי־יָמ֥וּךְ אָחִ֛יךָ עִמָּ֖ךְ וְנִמְכַּר־לָ֑ךְ לֹא־תַעֲבֹ֥ד בּ֖וֹ עֲבֹ֥דַת עָֽבֶד׃

i18n.en: And if your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not make him serve the service of a slave.

notes.official: *wənimkar-lāḵ* 'and sells himself to you'. *lōʾ-ṯaʿăḇōḏ bô ʿăḇōḏaṯ ʿāḇeḏ* 'you shall not make him serve the service of a slave' (ASV 'to serve as a bond-servant'). *ʿeḇeḏ* covers 'slave' and 'servant', and vv 39-55 argue with the word: no Israelite may be a human master's *ʿeḇeḏ*, because the Israelites are YHWH's *ʿăḇāḏîm* (vv 42, 55). The line uses 'slave' for the owned status and 'servants' for YHWH's claim (overlay `eved-amah-slave-servant-leviticus-25`).

paragraphs.text: כְּשָׂכִ֥יר כְּתוֹשָׁ֖ב יִהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֑ךְ עַד־שְׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל יַעֲבֹ֥ד עִמָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: As a hired worker, as a resident, he shall be with you; he shall serve with you until the year of jubilee.

notes.official: *kəśāḵîr kəṯôšāḇ* 'as a hired worker, as a resident': the impoverished Israelite works as a wage-earner, not as property, until the jubilee. Ex 21:2-6 and Deut 15:12-18 instead release the Hebrew debt-slave after six years. How the three laws relate is a classic problem of pentateuchal law (Milgrom, AB 3B; Levinson, *Deuteronomy and the Hermeneutics of Legal Innovation*, 1997).

paragraphs.text: וְיָצָא֙ מֵֽעִמָּ֔ךְ ה֖וּא וּבָנָ֣יו עִמּ֑וֹ וְשָׁב֙ אֶל־מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔וֹ וְאֶל־אֲחֻזַּ֥ת אֲבֹתָ֖יו יָשֽׁוּב׃

i18n.en: Then he shall go out from you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own family, and to the possession of his fathers he shall return.

notes.official: *wəʾel-ʾăḥuzzaṯ ʾăḇōṯāyw yāšûḇ* 'and to the possession of his fathers he shall return': the release of the person and the return of the land coincide in the jubilee.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־עֲבָדַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם לֹ֥א יִמָּכְר֖וּ מִמְכֶּ֥רֶת עָֽבֶד׃

i18n.en: For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Mitsrayim; they shall not be sold as a slave is sold.

notes.official: *kî-ʿăḇāḏay hēm ... lōʾ yimmāḵrû mimkereṯ ʿāḇeḏ* 'For they are my servants ... they shall not be sold as a slave is sold'. The same noun stands on both sides: the Israelites are YHWH's *ʿăḇāḏîm* because he brought them out of Egypt, the house of *ʿăḇāḏîm* (Ex 20:2), and so they cannot be sold as anyone else's *ʿeḇeḏ*. The line renders YHWH's claim with the corpus word 'servants' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS) and the sale with 'slave', and states the wordplay here (overlay `eved-amah-slave-servant-leviticus-25`). Alter prints 'my slaves', which keeps one English word on both sides.

paragraphs.text: לֹא־תִרְדֶּ֥ה ב֖וֹ בְּפָ֑רֶךְ וְיָרֵ֖אתָ מֵאֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: You shall not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your Elohim.

notes.official: *lōʾ-ṯirdeh ḇô bəp̄āreḵ* 'You shall not rule over him with harshness' (ASV 'with rigor'): *pereḵ* is the word for the Egyptian oppression (Ex 1:13-14), so the law forbids Israel to treat a fellow Israelite as Egypt treated Israel.

paragraphs.text: וְעַבְדְּךָ֥ וַאֲמָתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִהְיוּ־לָ֑ךְ מֵאֵ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֗ם אֲשֶׁר֙ סְבִיבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵהֶ֥ם תִּקְנ֖וּ עֶ֥בֶד וְאָמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And as for your male slave and your female slave whom you may have: from the nations that are around you, from them you may buy male and female slaves.

notes.official: *wəʿaḇdəḵā waʾămāṯəḵā* 'your male slave and your female slave', bought from the surrounding nations (overlay `eved-amah-slave-servant-leviticus-25`). The release laws of vv 39-43 apply only to Israelites.

paragraphs.text: וְ֠גַם מִבְּנֵ֨י הַתּוֹשָׁבִ֜ים הַגָּרִ֤ים עִמָּכֶם֙ מֵהֶ֣ם תִּקְנ֔וּ וּמִמִּשְׁפַּחְתָּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמָּכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹלִ֖ידוּ בְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם וְהָי֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם לַֽאֲחֻזָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And also from the children of the residents who sojourn with you, from them you may buy, and from their families that are with you, which they have begotten in your land; and they shall be your possession.

notes.official: *mibbənê hattôšāḇîm haggārîm ʿimmāḵem* 'from the children of the residents who sojourn with you' (overlay `ger-toshav-sojourner-resident-leviticus-25`). *wəhāyû lāḵem laʾăḥuzzâ* 'and they shall be your possession': *ʾăḥuzzâ*, the word for the family's land, here designates persons held as property (central `achuzzah-patriarchal-possession-holding-keyword`).

paragraphs.text: וְהִתְנַחֲלְתֶּ֨ם אֹתָ֜ם לִבְנֵיכֶ֤ם אַחֲרֵיכֶם֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֲחֻזָּ֔ה לְעֹלָ֖ם בָּהֶ֣ם תַּעֲבֹ֑דוּ וּבְאַ֨חֵיכֶ֤ם בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אִ֣ישׁ בְּאָחִ֔יו לֹא־תִרְדֶּ֥ה ב֖וֹ בְּפָֽרֶךְ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And you may leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, to hold as a possession; you may make them serve you forever. But over your brothers, the children of Yisra'el, you shall not rule, one over another, with harshness.

notes.official: *wəhiṯnaḥaltem ʾōṯām* 'and you may leave them as an inheritance'; *ləʿōlām bāhem taʿăḇōḏû* 'you may make them serve you forever'. The verse closes by repeating the prohibition of v 43 for Israelites.

paragraphs.text: וְכִ֣י תַשִּׂ֗יג יַ֣ד גֵּ֤ר וְתוֹשָׁב֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ וּמָ֥ךְ אָחִ֖יךָ עִמּ֑וֹ וְנִמְכַּ֗ר לְגֵ֤ר תּוֹשָׁב֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ א֥וֹ לְעֵ֖קֶר מִשְׁפַּ֥חַת גֵּֽר׃

i18n.en: And if a sojourner or resident with you prospers, and your brother beside him becomes poor and sells himself to the sojourner who is a resident with you, or to an offshoot of the sojourner's family,

notes.official: *gēr wəṯôšāḇ ʿimmāḵ* 'a sojourner or resident with you'; *ləḡēr tôšāḇ* 'to the sojourner who is a resident' (asyndetic pair); *ʿēqer mišpaḥaṯ gēr* 'an offshoot of the sojourner's family' (*ʿēqer* 'root, offshoot'). The case reverses vv 39-46: an Israelite sold to a non-Israelite keeps the right of redemption.

paragraphs.text: אַחֲרֵ֣י נִמְכַּ֔ר גְּאֻלָּ֖ה תִּהְיֶה־לּ֑וֹ אֶחָ֥ד מֵאֶחָ֖יו יִגְאָלֶֽנּוּ׃

i18n.en: after he is sold he shall have redemption; one of his brothers may redeem him,

notes.official: *gəʾullâ tihyeh-llô* 'he shall have redemption'. The redeemers are listed in order of kinship in vv 48-49 (central `goel-geullah-redeemer-redemption-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: אוֹ־דֹד֞וֹ א֤וֹ בֶן־דֹּדוֹ֙ יִגְאָלֶ֔נּוּ אֽוֹ־מִשְּׁאֵ֧ר בְּשָׂר֛וֹ מִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ יִגְאָלֶ֑נּוּ אֽוֹ־הִשִּׂ֥יגָה יָד֖וֹ וְנִגְאָֽל׃

i18n.en: or his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or any of his near kin of his family may redeem him; or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.

notes.official: *ʾô-miššəʾēr bəśārô mimmišpaḥtô* 'or any of his near kin of his family': literally 'the flesh of his flesh'. *ʾô-hiśśîḡâ yāḏô wəniḡʾāl* 'or if he prospers, he may redeem himself'.

paragraphs.text: וְחִשַּׁב֙ עִם־קֹנֵ֔הוּ מִשְּׁנַת֙ הִמָּ֣כְרוֹ ל֔וֹ עַ֖ד שְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֑ל וְהָיָ֞ה כֶּ֤סֶף מִמְכָּרוֹ֙ בְּמִסְפַּ֣ר שָׁנִ֔ים כִּימֵ֥י שָׂכִ֖יר יִהְיֶ֥ה עִמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he shall reckon with his buyer from the year that he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee; and the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years; as the days of a hired worker shall he be with him.

notes.official: The redemption price is the remaining years until the jubilee valued at a hired worker's wage (*kîmê śāḵîr*).

paragraphs.text: אִם־ע֥וֹד רַבּ֖וֹת בַּשָּׁנִ֑ים לְפִיהֶן֙ יָשִׁ֣יב גְּאֻלָּת֔וֹ מִכֶּ֖סֶף מִקְנָתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: If there are still many years, according to them he shall give back the price of his redemption out of the money for which he was bought.

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־מְעַ֞ט נִשְׁאַ֧ר בַּשָּׁנִ֛ים עַד־שְׁנַ֥ת הַיֹּבֵ֖ל וְחִשַּׁב־ל֑וֹ כְּפִ֣י שָׁנָ֔יו יָשִׁ֖יב אֶת־גְּאֻלָּתֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And if few years remain until the year of jubilee, then he shall reckon with him; according to his years he shall give back the price of his redemption.

paragraphs.text: כִּשְׂכִ֥יר שָׁנָ֛ה בְּשָׁנָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֣ה עִמּ֑וֹ לֹֽא־יִרְדֶּ֥נּֽוּ בְּפֶ֖רֶךְ לְעֵינֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: As a worker hired year by year he shall be with him; he shall not rule over him with harshness in your sight.

notes.official: *lōʾ-yirdennû bəp̄ereḵ ləʿêneyḵā* 'he shall not rule over him with harshness in your sight': the community is charged with seeing that the foreign master observes the law of v 43.

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־לֹ֥א יִגָּאֵ֖ל בְּאֵ֑לֶּה וְיָצָא֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת הַיֹּבֵ֔ל ה֖וּא וּבָנָ֥יו עִמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And if he is not redeemed by these means, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee, he and his children with him.

notes.official: *bəʾēlleh* 'by these means', i.e. by any of the forms of redemption in vv 48-49.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־לִ֤י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֲבָדִ֔ים עֲבָדַ֣י הֵ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אוֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: For to me the children of Yisra'el are servants; they are my servants whom I brought out of the land of Mitsrayim. I am YHWH your Elohim.'"

notes.official: *kî-lî ḇənê-yiśrāʾēl ʿăḇāḏîm ʿăḇāḏay hēm* 'For to me the children of Yisra'el are servants; they are my servants': the chapter's last word restates the ground of vv 39-54 (see v 42; overlay `eved-amah-slave-servant-leviticus-25`). The refrain *ʾănî YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵem* closes YHWH's speech and Moses' (opened at v 2).
